title: MEPS 2024 care delay connects to payment strategy, sacrifice, work constraints, and family care context
source_unit: MEPS 2024 person-level care-delay and ESAQ adaptation fields

observations.period: 2024; R4/2 cost-related care delay compared with R5/3 ESAQ adaptation

denominator.unit: ESAQ-weighted respondent groups with field-specific valid denominators

care_delay_to_adaptation.value: payment strategy, spending/savings sacrifice, work/leave constraint, and family-care profiles for care-delay groups

observations.method: Use ESAQWT24F and valid HC-256 R4/2 and ESAQ fields; profile respondents reporting or not reporting cost-related medical-care delay and inability to afford care.
observations.uncertainty: Care-delay and ESAQ fields are not a dated same-bill sequence; the same respondent may report different needs, and timing/causation/remedy are not identified.
observations.subgroup: MEPS 2024 respondents with valid ESAQ-weighted fields; care-delay groups retained separately.
observations.counterinterpretation: Health severity, income shocks, coverage, employment, recall, and common unmeasured causes can generate both delay and adaptation.

boundary: This is a same-respondent cross-round association between cost-related care delay and adaptation. It does not identify a dated episode, causal mediation, institutional repair, trust, political action, or geopolitical consequence.
